scope: the loading object is PARTIALLY INITIALISED: it contains 0xBAADF00D (the Microsoft uninitialised heap marker) and a repeated {4, 0.75, 3, pointer} record
why_this_matters: 0xBAADF00D is what the Microsoft debug heap fills freshly allocated memory with, so any field still holding it was never written
the object therefore has a repeated 16-byte record shape ({int 4, float 0.75, int 3, pointer}) that was written at least once, and adjacent slots that were not
that is direct evidence of an initialisation sequence that started and did not finish
which matches the observed behaviour exactly: the loader is alive, holds this object, and never proceeds
what_it_is_not: this is not the map fastfile loader itself (no filename strings appear in the object)
the repeated 4 / 0.75 / 3 record with 0xBAADF00D gaps looks more like a partially filled table of slots than a single load task
so the object may be a queue or a slot array whose remaining entries were never filled
the_next_step: find what writes the fields that ARE set (+0x0C = 4, +0x10 = 0.75, +0x14 = 3) by watching for a write to that address range
the writer's identity will say what kind of subsystem the object belongs to, and what the missing entries were supposed to be
